summary: Captures requirements for a service that would let people browse and search the IETF's mailing list archives using ordinary IMAP email clients. It is a requirements memo meant as input to a later design and development effort, not a protocol specification.

plainLanguage.summary: Lots of old group chat letters are stored somewhere. This lists what you would need so people could flip through them using their normal mail program.

questions: imap access to mailing list archives
how to search ietf email archives
subtitle: Browse IETF mailing list archives with your email client

tldr.problem: IETF participants want to search and browse archived email lists, but current web interfaces are limited.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC specifies requirements for an IMAP service that would expose IETF email archives as standard IMAP mailboxes, letting people use their normal email clients.
tldr.outcome: The document is a requirements memo intended to guide later design and development of such a service.

today: RFC 7017 remains an Informational Standard and has not been obsoleted. It guides implementation work for IETF email archive services.

sections.title: The Problem
sections.content: IETF participants rely on email lists to conduct work. The archives of those lists hold important history, but accessing them through web interfaces is cumbersome. This RFC captures requirements for a service that would let participants browse and search archives using standard IMAP clients, the protocol most people use for email.
sections.plainLanguage: IETF keeps old group emails. People want to search them with their regular mail program, not go to a web page.

sections.title: Key Requirements for the Service
sections.content:
The service must expose archives as standard IMAP mailboxes, with each email list as a mailbox. It must work with ordinary IMAP clients. Users with credentials should each have their own read/unread marks and annotations. Access control must prevent users from deleting, inserting or moving messages; the archive should be read-only.

The service must support server-side searching at scale, handle restricted archives via authentication, and allow anonymous access to open archives. It should consider IMAP extensions for sorting, threading, multi-mailbox search and fuzzy search.
sections.plainLanguage: The system has to let people read emails using mail programs, let them mark messages as read, but not let them delete or change the archives.

sections.title: Security and Performance
sections.content: Since searching can be resource-intensive, implementors must guard against denial-of-service attacks through maliciously crafted searches or many simultaneous connections. Storing annotations and read/unread marks requires storage space; implementors should rate-limit copying of messages and alert administrators when users consume exceptional storage.
sections.plainLanguage: Searches can use lots of computer power, so the system needs to stop bad searches and watch out for people taking up too much space.
